title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子

proposal.before: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."
proposal.after: When the emperor asked why, the crown prince replied, "At night, in a sudden crisis, one must guard against the unexpected; the ruler should not be illuminated where others can see him."
proposal.reason: Proposed source-backed correction; exact wording and downstream mentions require independent decision and reconciliation.

context.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
context.idiomatic: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.
context.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

context.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
context.idiomatic: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.
context.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

context.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
context.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."
context.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

context.zh: 由是奇之。
context.idiomatic: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.
context.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.

context.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
context.idiomatic: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
context.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'

proposal.before: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
proposal.after: He once told the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; the prince's good reputation spread throughout the realm.
proposal.reason: Proposed source-backed correction; exact wording and downstream mentions require independent decision and reconciliation.

context.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
context.idiomatic: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.
context.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

context.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」
context.idiomatic: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."
context.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'

context.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。
context.idiomatic: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
context.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

context.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
context.idiomatic: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
context.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

context.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
context.idiomatic: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
context.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

proposal.before: Empress Jia secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter the crown prince: "Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?"
proposal.after: Empress Jia had long resented the crown prince's good reputation, so she secretly instructed the Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: "Your Highness should indulge your desires while you are young. Why always restrain yourself?"
proposal.reason: Proposed source-backed correction; exact wording and downstream mentions require independent decision and reconciliation.

context.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
context.idiomatic: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
context.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

context.zh: 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅。
context.idiomatic: Adult Yu spurned books, slighted tutors, and played with pages.
context.literal: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.

context.zh: 賈后素忌太子有令譽，因此密敕黃門閹宦媚諛于太子曰：「殿下誠可及壯時極意所欲，何為恆自拘束？」
context.idiomatic: Empress Jia secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter the crown prince: "Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?"
context.literal: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'

context.zh: 每見喜怒之際，輒歎曰：「殿下不知用威刑，天下豈得畏服！」
context.idiomatic: Whenever she saw him angry or pleased she would sigh, "Your Highness does not know how to wield awe and punishment—how will the realm ever fear and obey!"
context.literal: Whenever she saw him angry or pleased she would sigh, 'Your Highness does not know how to wield awe and punishment—how will the realm ever fear and obey!'

context.zh: 太子所幸蔣美人生男，又言宜隆其賞賜，多為皇孫造玩弄之器，太子從之。
context.idiomatic: When Consort Jiang bore a son they pushed costly toys and stipends—Yu complied.
context.literal: When Lady Jiang, whom the crown prince favored, bore a son, they also said rewards should be lavish and many toys fashioned for the imperial grandson; the crown prince obeyed.
